Logan / Ben — draft materials attached. Quick summary of the core points you can include in the external response: 

1) Training on customer data
- Default behavior (hosted API): We do not use customer prompts or model outputs to train or fine-tune our models for product improvements. By default, customer content is excluded from any training corpus.
- Opt-in model: Customers can explicitly opt in to a program that allows aggregated, de-identified data to be used for model improvement; this is governed by an explicit contractual amendment and a documented consent flow. We do not accept opt-in via UI-only toggles — legal signature required.

2) Dedicated & Private deployments
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments are isolated: no off-cluster replication for training, and no telemetry used for model training. Customers can request on-site verification steps (SOW/inspection).

3) Retention & logging
- Short-term logs: prompt and response logs retained by default for 30 days for routing, abuse detection, and debugging; configurable down to 0 days for eligible enterprise accounts.
- Audit logs and billing traces: retained per customer contract; default 12 months for hosted tier, longer for Dedicated as agreed.
- Ephemeral mode: we provide options to mask or redact prompt tokens at ingestion and to disable transcript retention entirely for customers with strict requirements.

4) Evidence & artifacts attached
- redwood_no_train_attestation.pdf — signed attestation template stating default "no-train" practice and opt-in process.
- log_retention_playbook.pdf — operational playbook describing retention windows, purge procedures, and KMS key rotation for logs.
- CAIQ-complete.xlsx — completed CAIQ matrix with references to SOC 2 and DPIA docs.

Notes on language: Acme asked for "no-derive" language. We avoid absolute phrasing like "never"; instead we use contractually backed attestation that data is not used for model training unless the customer explicitly consents in writing. This gives legal cover and is consistent with our policy.

Attachments are stubbed in this thread; I recommend sending the attestation PDF and the CAIQ spreadsheet, and offering a short call if they want a line-by-line walkthrough.
